{\large Polynomial and Rational Functions}\par
\vspace{2pt}
{\small Ron Larson and Robert P. Hostetler, \emph{Precalculus with Limits}, 2nd ed., p. 125. Tick each box as you go.}\par
\vspace{6pt}
\begin{infobox}
Work through the four parts in order: read each section, practise the matching Duolingo units, work the book-only topics that Duolingo does not cover, then finish the chapter. Duolingo units are grouped by lane (a grade or a topic in the app) and listed in the order the app shows them, so you can follow one lane from top to bottom. \textbf{full} = the unit practises the section's main skill, \textbf{partial} = part of it, \textbf{prereq} = a warm-up from an earlier grade.

\textbf{In this chapter:} Grades 11 and 12 between them cover polynomial, complex, and rational functions thoroughly. Duolingo has no unit on polynomial long or synthetic division (2.3) or on nonlinear inequalities (2.7); use the book for those.

\section{3.\quad Section by section}
For each section: what Duolingo covers (the units are ticked off in part 2) and the book-only topics to work in the textbook. Tick each book-only topic once you have worked examples of it.
\subsection{2.1 Quadratic Functions and Models\tagright{p. 126}}
Thoroughly covered in grade 9 and the Algebraic Graphing topic. Completing the square to reach vertex form is lighter in the app.\par
{\small \textit{Duolingo:} \textbf{Grade 9:} 56. Tables of quadratic functions (full); 57. Graphs of quadratic functions (full); 58. Equations of quadratic functions (full); 59. Zeros of quadratic functions (full); 60. Factored form (full); 61. Vertex (full); 62. Vertex form (full)\\ \textbf{Algebraic Graphing:} 11. Intro to quadratic functions (full); 12. Quadratic graphs and equations (full); 13. Factored form of quadratics (full); 14. Vertex form of quadratics (full)}\par
{\small\textit{Book only:}}
\begin{checks}
  \item Completing the square to write vertex form
  \item Maximum and minimum word problems
\end{checks}
\subsection{2.2 Polynomial Functions of Higher Degree\tagright{p. 136}}
Grade 11 covers end behaviour, zeros, multiplicity, and relative extrema; grade 12 adds writing equations from graphs. The Leading Coefficient Test is taught as end behaviour.\par
{\small \textit{Duolingo:} \textbf{Grade 11:} 12. Intro to polynomial functions (full); 13. Relative maxima and minima of polynomial functions (full); 14. Zeros of polynomial functions (full); 15. Multiplicity of polynomial functions (full); 16. End behavior of odd polynomial functions (full); 17. End behavior of even polynomial functions (full)\\ \textbf{Grade 12:} 2. Polynomial function graphs (full); 5. Polynomial function equations from graphs (full); 48. Intermediate value theorem (partial)\\ \textbf{Algebraic Graphing:} 30. Polynomial function equations (full); 31. Polynomial function graphs (full); 32. Polynomial graphs and roots (full)}\par
{\small\textit{Book only:}}
\begin{checks}
  \item Using the Intermediate Value Theorem to locate a zero
\end{checks}
\subsection{2.3 Polynomial and Synthetic Division\tagright{p. 150}}
Duolingo has no unit on polynomial long division, synthetic division, or the Remainder and Factor Theorems. Use the book; grade 12's Rational root theorem assumes this skill.\par
{\small \textit{Duolingo:} no unit covers this section.}\par
{\small\textit{Book only:}}
\begin{checks}
  \item Polynomial long division
  \item Synthetic division
  \item The Remainder Theorem and the Factor Theorem
\end{checks}
\subsection{2.4 Complex Numbers\tagright{p. 159}}
Grade 11 covers the imaginary unit, arithmetic, conjugates, and powers of i. Division by a complex number is practised through conjugates; the complex plane is book only.\par
{\small \textit{Duolingo:} \textbf{Grade 11:} 18. The imaginary number, i (full); 19. Square roots of negative numbers (full); 20. Patterns of exponentiating i (full); 21. Multiply complex numbers (full); 23. Complex conjugates (full)}\par
{\small\textit{Book only:}}
\begin{checks}
  \item Plotting complex numbers in the complex plane
\end{checks}
\subsection{2.5 Zeros of Polynomial Functions\tagright{p. 166}}
Rational zero test, complex zeros, and conjugate pairs are covered across grades 11 and 12. Vieta's formulas go beyond the section. Descartes' Rule of Signs and bounds are book only.\par
{\small \textit{Duolingo:} \textbf{Grade 11:} 14. Zeros of polynomial functions (prereq); 22. Complex roots (full)\\ \textbf{Grade 12:} 3. Roots of polynomial functions (full); 4. Rational root theorem (full); 6. Vieta's formula for quadratic polynomials (partial); 7. Vieta's formula for cubic polynomials (partial)}\par
{\small\textit{Book only:}}
\begin{checks}
  \item The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
  \item Descartes's Rule of Signs
  \item Upper and lower bounds for real zeros
\end{checks}
\subsection{2.6 Rational Functions\tagright{p. 181}}
Very well covered. Grade 11 walks through intercepts and each kind of asymptote; grade 12 adds holes and slant asymptotes explicitly.\par
{\small \textit{Duolingo:} \textbf{Grade 11:} 24. Intro to rational functions (full); 25. Y-intercept of rational functions (full); 26. X-intercepts of rational functions (full); 27. Vertical asymptotes of rational functions (full); 28. Rewrite rational functions (full); 29. End behavior approaching a horizontal line (full); 30. End behavior approaching y=0 (full); 31. End behavior approaching slant asymptotes (full)\\ \textbf{Grade 12:} 8. Zeros of rational functions (full); 9. Vertical asymptotes of rational functions (full); 10. Horizontal asymptotes of rational functions (full); 11. Holes in rational functions (full); 12. Slant asymptotes of rational functions (full)\\ \textbf{Algebraic Graphing:} 33. Rational function equations and graphs (full); 34. Rewrite and graph rational functions (full); 35. Rational function asymptotes (full); 36. Holes and slant asymptotes (full)}\par
{\small\textit{Book only:}}
\begin{checks}
  \item Applications of rational functions
\end{checks}
\subsection{2.7 Nonlinear Inequalities\tagright{p. 194}}
Duolingo has no unit on polynomial or rational inequalities or the sign-chart method. Grade 9 one-variable inequalities are the only warm-up.\par
{\small \textit{Duolingo:} \textbf{Grade 9:} 11. Solve one-variable inequaltiies (prereq); 12. Compound 'or' inequalities (prereq); 13. Compound 'and' inequalities (prereq)}\par
{\small\textit{Book only:}}
\begin{checks}
  \item Polynomial inequalities
  \item Rational inequalities
  \item The test-interval (sign chart) method
\end{checks}
